user_task: Make routines of useful scraping APIs from the Premier League website
usage_guide:
This catalog provides routines for scraping key public APIs behind premierleague.com. Use them from a browser-like context (or any HTTP client that can send standard web headers) against the documented endpoints on api.premierleague.com and sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com.

Routines:
1) pl_standings — Fetch Premier League standings for a competition/season via Pulselive /api/v5/competitions/{competitionId}/seasons/{seasonId}/standings. Use when you need league tables and form breakdowns. Parameters: competitionId (int, e.g. 8 for PL), seasonId (int, e.g. 2025).

2) pl_fixtures_by_matchweek — Fetch fixtures for a given competition, season, and matchweek via Pulselive /api/v1/competitions/{competitionId}/seasons/{seasonId}/matchweeks/{matchweek}/matches or the generic /api/v2/matches with compSeasons, gameweeks, etc. Use when you need match lists or schedules by round.

3) pl_teams_list — Fetch list of teams for a competition/season via Pulselive /api/v1/competitions/{competitionId}/seasons/{seasonId}/teams. Use this first when you need team ids/names to feed into other routines.

4) pl_team_profile_bundle — Given a team id, combine: Pulselive team core (/api/v2/teams/{teamId} or /api/v2/teams-by-id?id={teamId}), metadata (/api/v1/metadata/SDP_FOOTBALL_TEAM/{teamId}), form and next fixture (/api/v1/competitions/{compId}/seasons/{seasonId}/teams/{teamId}/form and /nextfixture), plus promo/content from api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/PROMO/en with references to the team. Use when building a rich team page.

5) pl_player_profile_and_stats — Given playerId and season, call Pulselive /api/v1/players/{playerId} plus /api/v2/competitions/{compId}/seasons/{seasonId}/players/{playerId}/stats. Use for detailed player pages or comparison tools.

6) pl_match_detail — Given matchId, call Pulselive /api/v1/matches/{matchId}/events and /api/v3/matches/{matchId}/lineups. Use for timelines and lineup graphics.

7) pl_content_search — Use api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en with query parameters (contentTypes, page, pageSize, tagNames, flags) to search articles and videos. Use to surface general PL content.

8) pl_playlist_detail — Use api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/playlist/en/{playlistId} with optional pageSize/detail params to fetch curated content lists. Use for carousels and themed collections.

9) pl_video_detail — Use api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/VIDEO/en/{videoId} to fetch video metadata, and api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/photo/PHOTO/en/{photoId} for images. Use when embedding media.

10) pl_broadcast_schedule — Use api.premierleague.com/broadcasting/events and /broadcasting/match-events with dateFrom/dateTo, page, pageSize, and sportDataId filters to retrieve TV/broadcast schedules.

All core football-data and content endpoints observed are public GETs with no Authorization or cookies. In a browser, use window.fetch with default headers from a premierleague.com origin to avoid CORS issues; in non-browser clients, mimic a modern browser User-Agent and standard headers. Start with pl_teams_list and pl_standings to discover ids, then chain into team, player, match, and content routines as needed.
